instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In Joh 21:25 the supposing runs from the writer toward the many things Jesus did: it is a judgment of their extent.
observations.grounds: I suppose that the world itself could not contain

observations.text: In Act 17:29, Rom 2:3, 1Ti 6:5 and Jam 1:7 the view runs from people toward God, his judgment, godliness or what the Lord gives, and the verse turns it back: the divine is not like man's image, the judge will not escape, godliness is not gain, the doubter will not receive.
observations.grounds: that you will escape the judgment of God

observations.text: In Gen 18:30 and Gen 18:32 Abraham asks that the Lord not be angry before he puts the next case with suppose: the plea guards the putting of the case, and the anger is the Lord's that Abraham fears.
observations.grounds: Oh let not the Lord be angry

observations.text: In 1Ti 6:5 gain is the content of the false view: people depraved in mind imagine that godliness is a means of gain.
observations.grounds: godliness is a means of gain

observations.text: In Joh 11:31 the Jews who were consoling Mary in the house follow her out, supposing she goes to the tomb: the consoling is what they were doing when the supposing moved them.
observations.grounds: consoling her, saw Mary rise quickly

observations.text: In 2Sa 13:32 command is the word of Absalom by which the deed was set: Jonadab corrects the king's view by naming that the killing was by Absalom's command, from the day Tamar was violated. The pairing with command is through the code of saying (H0559) behind suppose.
observations.grounds: by the command of Absalom

observations.text: In Luk 7:43 Simon gives his view and Jesus says he has judged rightly: the supposing is weighed and found correct. In Rom 2:3 the one who judges others is asked whether he supposes he will escape: judging others stands against a false view of oneself.
observations.grounds: You have judged rightly

observations.text: In Act 14:19 the crowds, persuaded by the Jews from Antioch and Iconium, stone Paul and drag him out, supposing him dead: the persuading moves them to the act, and the supposing ends it.
observations.grounds: having persuaded the crowds

observations.text: In 2Sa 13:32 violated names the wrong done to Tamar, the cause Jonadab gives for Amnon's death against the king's fear that all his sons are dead.
observations.grounds: the day he violated his sister Tamar

observations.text: In 2Sa 13:32 determined names Absalom's purpose held since Tamar was violated: Jonadab sets this settled intent against the king's view.
observations.grounds: this has been determined

observations.text: In Joh 11:31 going is the content of the supposing: the Jews take Mary to be going to the tomb to weep there.
observations.grounds: she was going to the tomb

observations.text: In Jam 4:5 the readers are asked whether they suppose the Scripture speaks to no purpose, and what it says is that he yearns jealously over the spirit: the question presses them to take the yearning seriously.
observations.grounds: He yearns jealously over the spirit

observations.text: In Gen 18:28, Gen 18:31 and Gen 18:32 each case Abraham puts with suppose is answered on destroying: will you destroy the city, and the Lord says he will not destroy it for the sake of the number. The case is put to hold back destruction.
observations.grounds: For the sake of ten I will not destroy it

observations.text: In Act 16:27 the jailer supposes the prisoners have escaped and is about to kill himself: the false view nearly leads to his death. In Rom 2:3 the man who judges is asked if he supposes he will escape God's judgment: escape is the content of a false view in both.
observations.grounds: supposing that the prisoners had escaped

observations.text: In 1Ti 6:5 those who imagine godliness is gain have a corrupted mind and have lost the truth: the false view is set in a depraved mind.
observations.grounds: depraved in mind and deprived of the truth

observations.text: In Gen 18:28 lacking names the first case Abraham puts: suppose the fifty righteous lack five.
observations.grounds: Suppose five of the fifty righteous are lacking

observations.text: In Joh 11:31 the Jews followed Mary because of what they supposed: the following is the act that rests on the supposing.
observations.grounds: they followed her, supposing

observations.text: In 1Ti 6:5 godliness is what the false view is about: it is taken to be a way to gain, which the verse sets in minds deprived of the truth.
observations.grounds: imagining that godliness is a means of gain

observations.text: In 2Sa 13:33 the king is asked not to take the report to heart so as to suppose all his sons dead: the heart is where the false view would be taken up. In 1Ti 6:5 the mind of those who imagine godliness is gain is depraved: the mind is the seat of the false view.
observations.grounds: so take it to heart as to suppose

observations.text: In Act 13:25 John asks what they suppose him to be and says he is not worthy to untie the sandals of the one after him: the hearers' view of him is corrected by his own low counting of himself.
observations.grounds: What do you suppose that I am

observations.text: In Act 27:13 the sailors suppose they have obtained their purpose and set sail: the supposing is about an intent reached. In Jam 4:5 purpose is in the question whether the Scripture speaks for nothing.
observations.grounds: supposing that they had obtained their purpose

observations.text: In Jam 4:5 jealously names how he yearns over the spirit, the saying the readers are asked not to suppose empty.
observations.grounds: He yearns jealously over the spirit

observations.text: In 2Sa 13:32 killed is the content of the view the king is not to hold, that all the young men were killed. In Act 16:27 the jailer is about to kill himself because of what he supposes: the view leads to the act against himself.
observations.grounds: was about to kill himself

observations.text: In 1Cor 8:2 the one who imagines he knows something does not yet know as he ought: the imagining is a claim to knowing that the verse sets against true knowledge. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through think; the verse sets imagining against knowing.
observations.grounds: If anyone imagines that he knows something

observations.text: In Joh 11:31 the Jews suppose Mary goes to the tomb to weep, and in Joh 20:15 Mary, asked why she weeps, takes Jesus for the gardener: weeping is the setting of both supposings, and in Joh 20:15 the grief carries the mistaken view.
observations.grounds: Woman, why are you weeping

observations.text: Dead is the content of the view in 2Sa 13:32, 2Sa 13:33 and Act 14:19: the king fears all his sons are dead and is told only Amnon is, and the crowds take Paul for dead after stoning him. In each the view is mistaken.
observations.grounds: supposing that he was dead

observations.text: In Psa 41:7 the ones who imagine the worst for the psalmist are those who hate him: the devising of harm comes from hatred, with whispering together.
observations.grounds: All who hate me whisper together about me

observations.text: In Pro 18:11 strong describes the city the rich man takes his wealth to be: the strength is in his own picture, a high wall in his imagination.
observations.grounds: wealth is his strong city

observations.text: In Act 16:27 the jailer sees the prison doors open and from that supposes the prisoners have escaped: the sight is the ground of the view.
observations.grounds: saw that the prison doors were open

observations.text: In Gen 18:29 to Gen 18:32 each case Abraham puts with suppose is followed by the Lord's answer, and in Luk 7:43 Simon answers with his view: the supposing is spoken within an exchange. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through say; the codes of answer and suppose differ in Genesis.
observations.grounds: For the sake of forty I will not do it

observations.text: In Pro 18:11 wealth is what the rich man pictures as a strong city: the imagination is of what his riches are to him.
observations.grounds: like a high wall in his imagination

observations.text: In Gen 18:28 righteous names the people of Abraham's case, the fifty short by five. In 1Ti 6:5 truth is what those who imagine godliness is gain are deprived of.
observations.grounds: Suppose five of the fifty righteous are lacking

observations.text: In Gen 18:28 and Gen 18:30 find is the Lord's answer to Abraham's case: if he finds the number there, he will not destroy. In Luk 2:44 the parents, supposing the boy in the group, travel a day before they search for him, and in Joh 20:15 Mary, asked whom she seeks, takes Jesus for the gardener: the supposing delays or misdirects the seeking.
observations.grounds: they began to search for him

observations.text: In Gen 18:29 and Gen 18:30 do is the Lord's not doing what Abraham's case asks him to hold back. In Eze 18:14 the son of the case sees his father's sins and does not do likewise. In Rom 2:3 the one who judges does the same things and is asked if he supposes he escapes.
observations.grounds: he sees, and does not do likewise

observations.text: In Eze 18:14 the prophet's case is of a son who sees all the sins his father did: the sins are what the son sees and turns from.
observations.grounds: sees all the sins that his father has done

observations.text: In 2Sa 13:33 take is the setting of the heart on the report: the king is not to take it to heart so as to suppose all his sons dead. In Joh 20:15 Mary, taking Jesus for the gardener, offers to take the body away.
observations.grounds: so take it to heart as to suppose

observations.text: In Luk 7:43 rightly is Jesus' verdict on Simon's view: the supposing is judged correct.
observations.grounds: You have judged rightly

observations.text: In Psa 41:7 the haters whisper together against the psalmist and devise the worst for him: the whispering is the speech that goes with the devising, both turned against him.
observations.grounds: whisper together about me

observations.text: In Rom 2:3 judgment is God's, which the man who judges others is asked if he supposes he will escape: the false view is of escaping it.
observations.grounds: escape the judgment of God

observations.text: *enthymēsis / dianoēma* | Thoughts known by Jesus · thoughts and intentions discerned by the word · imagination that makes images of God | Mat 9:4; 12:25; Luk 11:17 · Heb 4:12 · Act 17:29 | "an image formed by the art and imagination of man" (Act 17:29). Imagination is the faculty of design (*ḥāšav* G) turned to making gods. This is the Greek counterpart of Hab 2:18 and the false likening of *dāmāh* (S/R)
